Re-running all five detectors against scratch_head_1010 at journal head shows the detection itself is wrong in two of three categories, and a named required input was never measured. (1) CLAIMED '9 duplicated foreign keys — same table, same columns, same parent' (finding F6, P2). MEASURED 0: `GROUP BY conrelid, confrelid, conkey HAVING count(*)>1` returns zero rows repo-wide, and the specific constraint it names, `fin_reimbursement_batches_approved_by_fkey`, does not exist — fin_reimbursement_batches carries 7 FKs, none duplicated. (2) CLAIMED '12 prefix-overlapping indexes ... all 12 must be classified KEEP', naming calendar_events, chat_channel_members x3, contacts x2, hr_people, inv_locations, inv_stock_levels x2, inv_stock_transactions, organization_people. MEASURED 37 pairs (same relation, same access method, same predicate, narrow key set a strict leading prefix of the wide one). The prior list is a subset; it misses acc_asset_categories, acc_tax_codes, accounting_settings, billing_profiles, chat_org_settings x2, crm_quote_settings, deals, employee_salary_profiles, fin_bank_accounts, gl_periods, health_score_config, hr_employments, inv_settings, kb_settings, org_ai_credits, payroll_policies x2, payroll_tds_ytd_ledger and others. NOTE: my first pass sliced indkey 1-based and returned 0; indkey::int2[] has lower bound 0 (verified: array_lower = 0) and the corrected query returns 37. (3) CLAIMED '0 true exact duplicate indexes'. Strictly TRUE — grouping on (relation, indkey, indoption, predicate, AM, indisunique) returns 0. But relaxing only sort direction and uniqueness returns 2 real overlaps: crm_commission_assignments has `idx_..._lookup (org_id, user_id, effective_from DESC)` beside `uniq_..._start UNIQUE (org_id, user_id, effective_from)`, and crm_commission_plan_versions the same shape — a non-unique btree fully served by a unique btree that differs only in trailing sort direction. (4) The criterion names four inputs; 'workload/index statistics' was never measured and CANNOT be here: pg_stat_statements is not installed on this server (`select count(*) from pg_extension where extname='pg_stat_statements'` = 0) and only 200 of 4,759 entries in pg_stat_user_indexes have idx_scan > 0, all from seeding and probes. The prior report is right that statistics could only ever add a KEEP — but the criterion requires the detection to use them, so the clause is unmet regardless of which direction it would move a verdict. The conservation half of the criterion ('preserve every constraint/index required for tenant isolation') does hold at head: nothing in the overlap sets has been dropped.
criteria.blocker: Workload/index statistics require pg_stat_statements plus index-scan counters from a production or staging replica over a representative window. Neither exists on this machine.
criteria.clauses_failing: Detection is neither complete nor accurate (0 duplicate FKs not 9; 37 prefix overlaps not 12; 2 direction-only index overlaps not 0) AND the 'workload/index statistics' input was never measured.

criteria.evidence: The removal half has not been performed and cannot be arbitrated at head. Backend `check:openapi-coverage` is a REAL VIOLATION (exit 1 in GATE-STATUS.tsv); /tmp/beg-check_openapi-coverage.log lists operation after operation as '2xx response (200) declares no content schema — a bare auto-generated key is not a contract' and ends '... and 3591 more'. I measured openapi.json directly at head: 3,648 operations; 1,385 (37.97%) carry a JSON request schema; 3,647 declare some 2xx; but only 26 (0.71%) carry a 2xx JSON response schema, over 6 components.schemas. Frontend `pnpm check:response-contracts` exits 0 but only as a freeze — 'Seam calls scanned: 2666 · Carrying a contract: 86 (3.2%) · Unparsed: 2580 (baseline 2594)' and it prints its own verdict: 'NOTE: 97.8% of the seam is still an unchecked cast. This gate freezes that debt; it does not retire it.' So removing a response field from a backend DTO is invisible to check:contract-breaking-change and reaches the frontend as an unchecked cast — 'one contract change' has no arbiter. No unused DTO/Zod field removal has in fact been executed. The PROTECTIVE half of the criterion does hold where a contract exists: check:contract-registry exits 0 and the 102 published operations carry a version/deprecation window, named consumer and idempotency rule. Note the prior report's figures (3,642 ops / 20 with a 2xx schema / 0.55%) are stale; head is 3,648 / 26 / 0.71% — the conclusion is unchanged.
criteria.blocker: The response half of the API contract does not exist (26 of 3,648 operations). Populating 2xx response schemas — ticket 04's territory — is the prerequisite before any field removal can be made and verified as one contract change.
criteria.clauses_failing: 'Remove unused request/response/DTO/Zod fields ... as one contract change' — no removal performed, and check:openapi-coverage is exit 1 at head so the change could not be detected. The protective clause (never remove tenant/actor, idempotency/version, authorization, audit or published-consumer fields without a migration path) holds.
